ns2:section.sectionText: This course explores the complex engagements of anthropologists with issues involving social inequality, poverty and racism, How do anthropologists who choose to undertake activism effectively intervene in public and policy debates to address observable injustices? What are the implications of such interventions? We will explore the disciplines legacies and currents such as applied and public anthropologies, postcolonial, feminist, and other approaches. What are the ethical implications, politically, theoretically, and socially, of what is now called "engaged anthropology"? This course will have an activist research component that will allow us to think about these issues beyond the walls of the academy.
